title: 3 Step BEGINNER Scalping Strategy (500 Trade BACKTEST)

strategies.name: engulfing_pattern_range_breakout_1h_5m

entry_sequence.action: Wait for a bullish engulfing pattern to form on the 7:00 a.m. candle and a bearish engulfing pattern to form on the 8:00 a.m. candle before the trading session.
entry_sequence.rationale: These patterns establish the session direction (bullish or bearish).

entry_sequence.action: On the 5-minute timeframe, mark the range from 9:30 to 9:45 UTC-4 (the first 15 minutes of the NYSE open).
entry_sequence.rationale: This defines the trading range for the session.

entry_sequence.action: Enter long when price breaks and closes outside the range high, or enter short when price breaks and closes outside the range low.
entry_sequence.rationale: The break of the range confirms momentum in the desired direction.

stop.rationale: The stop is placed below the range low for long trades and above the range high for short trades.

strategies.stop_management: Set break even once the trade reaches a certain level (implied by the speaker's example).

targets.rationale: The speaker aims for a risk-reward of approximately 2.16 to 2.3.

speaker_concepts.verbatim_description: I want to see a bullish engulfing pattern form before my trading session.
And if I want to sell, I want to see a bearish engulfing pattern form before my trading session.
I'm marking out the top and the bottom of that range from 9:30 to 9:45. That's the first 15 minutes of the New York Stock Exchange open, and that is my trading range for this trading session.
I'm simply looking for the price to break and close outside of that range as my next confirmation that I want to buy. This break of the range tells me the buyers have some momentum.
On this trading position, we have a level of demand off of this candle right here... And a level of demand is just when you have an aggressive push like you have right here.

This is a supply zone right there, and I put this around right about there in the middle of that supply because you know, if price comes up to supply, it very likely can react and come down off of that level.
You get the break of recent structure, and generally we're looking for fair value gaps, that sort of thing. And then we're waiting for a price retracement.
This is one of the main orb entry models that I use in my trading, especially when step one was so clear.
